themes.title: Capacity handling
mainQuestions: Look at the check at the top of push. Explain what it protects against and what the caller sees when it triggers.
In main, the for loop pushes six values. Predict which pushes succeed and what is printed for the others.
criteria: Student explains that the check prevents writing past the end of the data array and that push returns false when the stack is full
Student predicts that the first four pushes succeed and the fifth and sixth report that the stack is full

rubric.text: Says the check prevents writing past the end of the data array (out of bounds).
Says that push returns false when the stack is full, which is what the caller sees.
Says that the first four pushes (10 to 40) succeed.
Says that the fifth and sixth pushes fail and main prints "Full at 5" and "Full at 6".

themes.title: Index bookkeeping
mainQuestions: Look at how top is used inside pop. Explain why the value is read before top changes.
criteria: Student explains that top is the index of the most recent element, so the value is read from data[top] first and top is decremented afterwards

rubric.text: Says that top is the index of the most recent element.
Says that the value is read from data[top] before top is decremented, or why the order matters.
Says that decrementing top afterwards is what removes the item from the stack.

themes.title: Tracing the program
mainQuestions: Trace the while loop in main. In what order are the values printed, and why?
What does size() return at the end of main, and how is that number computed?
criteria: Student states that the values print as 40 30 20 10 because the last value pushed is the first one popped
Student says size returns 0 because top is back at -1 after four pops, and that top + 1 is the item count

rubric.text: Explains why: the last value pushed is the first one popped (last in, first out).
Gives the result: size returns 0 at the end of main and main prints "Size: 0".
Says that size returns top + 1, the item count, because top is an index and one less than the number of items.
Says that top is back at -1 after all four values were popped.

fixedFollowUps: What could go wrong in main if push did not return false when the stack was full?
What is stored in the stack once the for loop in main has finished?
What would pop return if top were decremented before the value was read?
Which value is removed first by the first successful call to pop in main?
What would size() return right after the for loop, before the first pop?
